documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34 y/o man establishing care. Lives in Deerfield; prior PCP too far to keep. Feels well, no complaints today. Works construction, long days on his feet.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none, no supplements. NKDA.
FH: father T2DM; mother HTN.
SH: single. Never smoker, 1-2 drinks a week, no drug use. Exercises regularly.
Outside records reviewed: healthy, Tdap 2014, labs 2022 normal.

ROS: negative in full except as above.

Exam: well-appearing, vitals reviewed. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin: no rashes. Ext: no edema. Neuro grossly normal. PHQ-2 is 0.

Assessment/plan, preventive care, healthy adult:
- Tdap due (last 2014), given. Flu shot given.
- Screening labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c given dad's diabetes, hep C antibody once.
- Discussed sun protection at work, hearing protection on site, lifting form.
- Annual physical next year.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mason, everything from Tuesday came back fine. Kidney and liver tests normal, blood counts normal, cholesterol in a good range, and your A1c shows no sign of diabetes. Hep C screen negative. Nothing to do until next year's physical. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Rash on feet
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey, I've had a rash on both feet for a few weeks now. Itches and burns, worse at night after I take my boots off. Tried some spray from the drugstore, didn't do much. Any chance I could be seen next week? Mornings work best.

documents.title: RE: Rash on feet
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Mason, we have Tuesday 8/5 at 7:30 am open with the doctor. You're booked. Please wear socks you can take off easily.

medications.sig: Apply thinly to affected areas of both feet twice daily for 4 weeks

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: Foot Rash
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Several weeks of an itchy rash on both feet with a burning quality. Clearly worse after a full shift in work boots, says his feet are soaked by the end of the day. Drugstore spray didn't help. No new soaps or detergents. No fever.
Meds none. NKDA.

O: Vitals fine. Both feet: red, scaly skin with fissures in the toe webs. Soles and the lateral borders thickened and scaly, moccasin pattern. No blisters, no pustules. No cellulitis, no lymphangitic streaking.
KOH prep done here from toe-web and sole scrapings: branched, segmented hyphae on the slide.

A: Tinea pedis, bilateral, interdigital and moccasin type, KOH positive.

P:
- Terbinafine 1% cream BID x 4 weeks, rub in beyond the edge of the rash. Keep going a week or so after it looks clear.
- Moisture-wicking socks, change midday, alternate two pairs of boots so each dries out, powder in boots.
- Message me in a few weeks on how it's going.

documents.title: Feet update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Cream is working. Itching mostly gone, skin between the toes looks almost normal. Still a little flaky on the bottoms. Bought a second pair of boots.

documents.title: RE: Feet update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great to hear. Finish the full four weeks plus another week past when the soles look clear. The thick skin on the soles is the slowest part to settle. Keep up the dry-feet routine.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt phoned, crew is starting a pour early tomorrow and he can't get off. Cancelled 9/23 physical. Rebooked Tues 10/7 8:00.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
35 y/o M here for yearly physical. Doing well. Feet: finished the terbinafine cream in early September, itch gone, says they're much better.

Meds: none currently. NKDA.
Social unchanged: construction, never smoker, 1-2 drinks/wk. Running most mornings before work.

ROS negative.

Exam: vitals reviewed, BMI normal. General well. HEENT, neck normal. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Feet: faint residual scale on the soles, toe webs clean and dry, no fissures. No other rash. PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
- Health maintenance up to date. Labs last fall all normal; none needed today.
- Flu vaccine given. Declined a COVID booster this season.
- Tinea pedis improving. If the itch returns, message me and I'll send more cream.
- See him in a year.

medications.sig: Apply to affected areas of both feet twice daily for 2 to 4 weeks

documents.title: Athlete's foot again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Feet started itching again last week, same spots between the toes. Can you send more of that cream? Same pharmacy.

documents.title: RE: Athlete's foot again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent a new tube of terbinafine cream to your pharmacy. Twice a day, and this time keep it up a full two weeks after it looks clear. If it keeps coming back we can look at other options.

orders.reason: Recurrent rash of groin and feet despite antifungal creams

documents.title: Rash in groin
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Kind of embarrassing but I've had an itchy red rash in my groin since around the beginning of October. I've been using the store-brand antifungal cream and it clears up, then a few weeks after I stop it's right back. Feet keep doing the same thing too. Is there something stronger, or should I see someone?

documents.title: RE: Rash in groin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not embarrassing at all, this is common, especially with the feet already involved. Since it keeps coming back after good courses of cream, I'd like dermatology to take a look and possibly culture it. I've put the referral in; our front desk will call you with a time. Until then keep the area dry and use the cream as you have been.

documents.title: Referral scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Referral and last two visit notes faxed to outside dermatology. They offered Mon 2/9 at 9:40. Called pt, confirmed. He'll bring his insurance card.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily for 14 days

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group
Date of service: 02/09/2026
Re: Mason Dean, DOB 10/18/1989
Referring: primary care physician

Thank you for sending Mr. Dean, a 36-year-old construction worker, for a rash in the groin.

History: For about four months he has had an itchy, red rash in both groin folds. Over-the-counter antifungal cream settles it each time, but it returns within a few weeks of stopping. He had a foot rash evaluated by your office in August 2025 (KOH positive at that visit) and reports athlete's foot treated several times over the past year. He denies new sexual partners and has not changed soaps, detergents or other hygiene products.

Medications: none at present (intermittent OTC antifungal cream).
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
PMH: tinea pedis. PSH: none.
Family history: father with type 2 diabetes; mother with hypertension.
Social: construction work, boots all day. Never smoker. Alcohol 1-2 drinks weekly.

Examination: Bilateral inguinal folds with sharply bordered, erythematous, scaly plaques. Feet show scale and maceration in the toe-web spaces bilaterally. Toenails are thickened and discolored. No inguinal or other lymphadenopathy. Remainder of the skin examined is clear.

Studies today: CBC within normal limits. HIV antigen/antibody negative. Fungal culture of a groin scraping sent; result to follow.

Impression:
1. Tinea cruris, recurrent.
2. Tinea pedis, recurrent, likely the reservoir for the groin.

Plan:
- Terbinafine 250 mg by mouth once daily for 14 days.
- Dry the groin thoroughly after showering; put socks on before underwear so the feet don't seed the groin; loose cotton underwear; separate towel for the feet.
- Absorbent antifungal powder in boots.
- We will forward the culture result.

Follow-up with us as needed.

Dermatology

documents.title: Dermatology addendum: fungal culture
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Addendum to consultation of 02/09/2026, Mason Dean.

Fungal culture, skin scraping, right and left inguinal folds: Trichophyton rubrum isolated (final 03/04/2026).

Consistent with the clinical diagnosis of tinea cruris. He has completed the prescribed terbinafine course. No change to the plan.

documents.title: All cleared up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to let you know the pills worked. Groin and feet both totally clear since about a week after I finished. Doing the powder and socks thing.

documents.title: RE: All cleared up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it, and thanks for the update. I saw the dermatology letter and the culture, which grew the usual fungus behind athlete's foot and jock itch. Keep the prevention habits going, especially through the summer.

documents.title: RE: Feet again
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Friday 7/31 at 7:15 am works. See you then.

medications.sig: Apply to the toe webs and surrounding skin of both feet twice daily for 2 weeks

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: Recurrent Tinea Pedis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mason is back with two weeks of itching between the toes on both feet. Notices it most after his morning run. He'd been completely clear since the oral terbinafine in February. No travel, no one sick at home. Groin fine. Not taking any medications. NKDA.

Exam: vitals unremarkable. Both feet: redness, scale and soggy white maceration in the toe webs, most marked in the 4th-5th spaces. Soles look clean this time. No vesicles, no pustules, no cellulitis. Inguinal skin clear.
KOH from the web spaces: branching hyphae.

Assessment: tinea pedis, recurrence, interdigital.

Plan:
- Terbinafine 1% cream BID x 2 weeks.
- Running shoes are probably the new culprit: dry them out between runs, swap socks right after, powder.
- If it keeps recurring we can talk with dermatology about a longer plan.
- Message me if not clearly better in two weeks.

documents.title: Foot follow-up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Two weeks in on the cream. Way better, just a little peeling between the last toes. Should I keep going?

documents.title: RE: Foot follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, keep going another week past the point it looks normal, then stop. The peeling is the skin healing. Let me know if it comes back.
